phase.label: Early career: the return to Bergholt, 1802

source.label: Wikipedia: “In 1802 he refused the position of drawing master … to become a professional landscape painter”
Museum record (Wikidata): oil paint on canvas
Wikipedia: “an 1802 landscape painting by the British artist John Constable”

work.text: Although Constable displayed an untitled landscape at the Royal Academy Exhibition of 1802 at Somerset House, his exhibition debut, it is not known whether this was the work in question.
In 1828 Constable produced a painting with a similar view The Vale of Dedham which is now in the Scottish National Gallery.

moment.text: There is little or nothing in the exhibition worth looking up to. There is room enough for a natural painter. The great vice of the present day is bravura, an attempt to do something beyond the truth.
moment.lead: Writing from London after the 1802 Academy exhibition:

source.author: John Constable
source.title: Letter to John Dunthorne, 29 May 1802, in C. R. Leslie, Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

moment.text: His early style has many qualities associated with his mature work, including a freshness of light, colour and touch, and reveals the compositional influence of the old masters he had studied, notably of Claude Lorrain.

matters.text: I shall return to Bergholt, where I shall endeavour to get a pure and unaffected manner of representing the scenes that may employ me.

source.author: John Constable
source.title: Letter to John Dunthorne, 29 May 1802, in C. R. Leslie, Life and Letters of John Constable, R.A. (1896 ed.)

matters.text: it was fortunate for him that he began with Claude and Girtin.
